newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-CommBank seen a buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-CommBank seen a buy.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia Ltd (CBA) has received a buy recommendation from Morgan Stockbroking Ltd who point to the bank's attractive dividend yield and potential for an improvement in earnings per share.
"The dividend yield is attractive and cost savings together with benefits of the share buy-back should sustain dividend growth," Morgan analyst Greg Cathro said in a report.
Cathro said as a result of the buy-back of 10 percent of the bank's own shares, earnings per share could improve by about five percent in the 1996/97 financial year.
"Using the current 78 percent dividend payout, this would represent a four to five percent increase in the annual dividend."

The Australian banking environment was currently characterised by intense competition and the Commonwealth Bank had become active in defending and increasing its strong retail lending presence, Cathro said.
"It (the bank) has a solid capital adequacy position from which to compete and to date during calendar 1996, its aggressive market response has led to an improved market share," Cathro said.
During the year ended June 30, 1996, the bank cut branch numbers by 84 to 1,390 while the number of automatic teller machines (ATM's) jumped by 470 and the number of EFTPOS terminals doubled.

The recent introduction of retirement savings accounts may offer a new long-term source of funding for the banking industry while the forthcoming government report into the finance industry could open Commonwealth Bank to takeover speculation, Cathro said.

"Management is forecasting a flat 1996/97 earnings result due to the reduction in home lending margins, its limited capacity to recover costs for retasil services and the funding cost of the recent buy-back," Cathro said.
Commonwealth Bank shares were 16 cents higher at A$11.11 at 12.55 p.m. (0255 GMT).
